To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The CMS DDT procedure was successful in delivering one by one working production transfer routes to CMS data operations team; (2) The CMS DTT procedure was successful in commissioning all crucial data transfer routes among the CMS computing centres; (3) The CMS DDC procedure was successfully used by the CMS data operations group in commissioning the CMS production data transfer routes; (4) The CMS DDD procedure was successfully used to commission the CMS production data transfers routes;
the debugging of the CMS data transfer links was a success.

the DDT taskforce was able to successfully debug and commission the majority of the data transfer routes between CMS computing centres, with the exception of the links to CERN, where the debugging is still in progress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the debugging of data transfer links in a distributed system such as the WLCG, and the experience and lessons learned in this process.

a study on how a task force of experts from the CMS experiment was created and how it was organized in order to successfully debug and commission data transfer routes among the computing centres which support the CMS experiment.

the development and deployment of the Load Test infrastructure for the CMS experiment, the experience gained in the debugging data transfer links within the CMS computing environment and the development of tools and techniques which can be useful for other experiments in LHC computing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CMS experiment has a well established debugging data transfer infrastructure which has been used to successfully commission all the most important data transfer links among CMS computing centres.
the CMS experiment has a working infrastructure to debug data transfers and a well-defined procedure to commission the links.
the debugging procedure was successful in commissioning all links among CMS computing centres and in providing a solid basis for the data operations team to take over the links and to maintain them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CMS experiment has successfully commissioned all data transfer routes among its computing centres, including the most critical routes, and has achieved a stable data transfer system in the WLCG environment.

the DDT taskforce was a successful experiment-wide activity which helped to debug and commission the data transfer routes in CMS and to provide the necessary tools for future debugging activities in the CMS experiment.
we have been able to commission most crucial data transfer routes in the CMS computing infrastructure, and have developed a procedure to debug data transfers in a systematic and efficient way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the debugging of data transfer links is a complex and time-consuming activity which requires dedicated resources.
debugging data transfer links is a challenging task which requires a systematic and well-organized approach, as well as a strong coordination between different groups and individuals.
the debugging of data transfer links is a long term activity that should be performed in a structured and systematic manner.
